MY PATTERN STUDIO

How to Make a Pattern

Choose two pieces, lay down your repeat and keep it going.

Look, then try.

The picture shows one way to begin. Pick two pieces that look different, such as a pink circle and a yellow square. Lay them down as your repeating part, then place the same two pieces again, and again. Say your pattern out loud while you point: circle, square, circle, square. Hearing the rule helps you predict the next piece. Your pieces can be anything that differs, such as two colours, two shapes, or a big piece and a small one.

Start drawing and writing below

Open the worksheet to print or save

An adult helps with cutting the pattern cards. Keep paper scraps away from younger children. Move gently during movement patterns: seated movements work too, and no jumping is needed.

Use a finger, stylus or mouse in each drawing box. Type below it, or ask a grown-up to write your words. Your work stays in this tab. Save before refreshing or leaving.

ACTIVITY 1

Choose two pieces

Draw the two pieces you picked. Make them look different from each other.

ACTIVITY 2

Make your repeat

Draw your repeating part. Then draw it again beside it.

ACTIVITY 3

Say it aloud

Point and say your pattern to a grown-up or to yourself. Then draw what would come next.

Your ideas belong here. There is no score.

What are we learning?

A repeating pattern grows from a small unit that returns in the same order. Saying the rule aloud helps you predict what comes next, and prediction is where early algebra begins.
